title: Good app, but just got aggressive
body:
I’ve been using HabitBull for a year now to help manage long projects (like reading every book I own, keep room clean, etc.). I’ve often wanted to upgrade but my finances are not at a place where I can justify in app purchases. 

So I resolved to use the free version until I pay off all my debt and get to a place where I’m comfortable spending. 

This last week, the app got really aggressive. I opened it to check off that I cleaned my room and it gave me a pop up asking me to buy it. Okay, I thought, can’t fault it for trying. I clicked on the x at the top, but instead of giving me the data screen, it acted like I’d tried to make a purchase. I cancelled it and it said purchase failed, but the screen stayed up, preventing me from entering my data for the day.  (Several hours later I managed to enter the data before I got the pop up again, with the same issue)

I’m hoping this is just a glitch, and will soon be fixed, not a punishment for longtime users who haven’t upgraded. 

Other positives about the app. I love that it lets you backtrack or go ahead. When one of my goals is to read a chapter a day, it’s nice to be able to make up days when I couldn’t get to it, or read ahead in anticipation of a family gathering/job/ class where I know I won’t have time.

I looked through about 6 or 7 popular habit apps and this one seemed to have the best/easiest visual showing percentage adherence to goals based on various denominators ((day,week, month). I’m not far into my 80/20 experiment, but this app seems to be the easiest for assessing adherence in such a way. I will say that entering each habit was a bit of a pain, but it is completely customizable so that is great.

title: Goal tracking numbers flawed
body: I like the simplicity, but there is an error tracking goals with number requirements. When setting goals, you choose yes/no (you did it or did not do it) or number goals (you track a specific number of something). When you set a number goal, the default is “not more than” so you can put something like consume “not more than” 1500 calories. When the app actually creates the goal, it switches “not more than” to “at least”. So now the goal is only accomplished if you eat 1500 calories OR MORE. I have written to them at least 3 times and have only gotten an automated response. The problem may be corrected in the paid version, but I won’t risk spending money on the paid one if the free one works this poorly and I can’t get support for the problem.

title: Awesome - but a minor bug with a workaround
body:

But there is a minor bug.  When you choose a numeric goal, you are given a choice for success.   It is either to perform above target (over 5 miles a day), exactly at target, or under target (less than 2 drinks a day).  
Unless you scroll through the options (roll up or down in the field) it may give you the wrong choice when you click save.

title: Love it!
body:
I missed this app a lot when I switched over from Android, I’d check the App Store for it every so often until it finally appeared! I’ve been loving it ever since. I use it to keep track of all sorts of things. From personal habits to things I want to know whether I did or not and ask myself when the last time that thing happened was. It’s incredibly flexible and I love that I can go into the daily checklist and check off any of the things and easily see which ones are truly daily and due today and which ones I just need to update. I love being able to see the multiple views for daily, weekly, and monthly. My favorite is being able to check off something or if I’m wondering the last time I did something was, I can click it and it’ll take me to the month view so I can see at a glance. It’s extremely helpful in letting me see when the last I watered my plant was and more. I have reminders set for a few of them, and I love being able to confirm it on my Apple Watch when the alert pops up! 

The only things that would make me love this app even more are:

1. Apple Watch app with a complication so I can easily tap and check things off my daily list. 
2. A year view for each. This would be incredible to be able to see long-term trends without having to navigate between months.

Thank you again for all of your hard work! I looove this app so much! :)

author: Steve N Koch

title: Excellent app, with great potential
body: I've tried a lot of habit tracking/forming apps, and haven't liked any of them as much as I like HabitBull. The best part is the complete flexibility and customizability. I haven't found a format I can't do with this app yet. The UI is simple and clean, if not astounding aesthetically, and it's easy to use. The upgrade is worth it. Not to mention the encouraging little messages that pop up sometimes. The creator is very helpful and I'm happy to provide my support. I look forward to using HabitBull over the next few months to see how I do with it.
